detailed_findings.finding: Correctly fixes an arbitrary positive integer d and proves the target inequality for that d, then quantifies over all positive integers d at the end.
The split of {1,...,b} into {1,...,a} and {a+1,...,b} is used appropriately, including the edge cases where one part is empty.
The bijection i -> r+i from {a+1,...,b} to the interval of integers r+a < m <= r+b is exactly the right translation to convert the count into M_d(r+a,r+b).

reason: The proof is a complete direct counting argument. For fixed positive d, it partitions the index set {1,...,b} into {1,...,a} and {a+1,...,b}, uses the definition e_i=i on the first part and e_i=r+i on the second, and identifies the second-part count with M_d(r+a,r+b). Doing the same for divisibility of i identifies the comparison count with M_d(a,b). The assumed inequality then gives the desired result. The proof matches the lemma statement and assembly role, and it uses no undeclared or forbidden dependencies.
